title: Testing with Postman
idea: Postman is a graphical API client: you build a request, send it to your running server, and read the status, headers and body of the reply.
points: Pick a method, enter a URL, send, then read the response pane.
The response pane shows status, time, size, body, headers and cookies.
Postman sets some headers itself, such as `Content-Type` for a raw JSON body.
Save requests in a collection; keep the server address in an environment variable.

code.caption: A stand-in server, with `fetch` playing Postman. The Body type decides the header, and the header decides parsing.

walk.text: A stand-in server. `express.json()` parses `application/json` bodies only.
The route logs the header and the body it received.
`send` builds the request. The body type becomes the `Content-Type` header.
Raw JSON in Postman sends this header.
Raw Text sends `text/plain`, which the JSON parser skips.
Close the server so the script can exit.

pitfalls: A route made with `app.post` answers `GET` with 404; set the method to match.
A wrong port gives a connection error, not a 404: check `baseUrl` against your `PORT`.
A request that works in Postman can still fail in a browser: Postman ignores CORS.

quiz.q: In the snippet, what does the second `send` log?
quiz.why: `express.json()` parses only `application/json`. For `text/plain` it skips the body, so `req.body` stays `undefined`.

takeaway: Postman fills in the same HTTP request any client would send.
